knowledge:
- key_parameters: input=The input SingleCellExperiment object to be classified ;; ref_cells=The reference SingleCellExperiment object containing annotated cell types ;; interm=Logical parameter in PlotCHETAH; if TRUE, colors intermediate types instead of final types ;; return_col=Logical parameter in PlotCHETAH; if TRUE, returns the color mapping ;; tree=Logical parameter in PlotCHETAH; if FALSE, suppresses plotting of the classification tree ;; confidence threshold=Numeric value passed to Classify (default 0.1) controlling classification stringency ;; whichnode=Integer node number in RenameBelowNode to target for renaming ;; replacement=Character string in RenameBelowNode specifying the new name for the node's descendants ;; n_genes=Parameter in CHETAHclassifier (default 200) specifying the number of genes used for classification
- alternatives: Seurat (mentioned for downstream visualization and color usage) ;; Other scRNA-seq classification methods (generic mention for optimization)
- when_to_use: When classifying cell types in scRNA-seq query data using an annotated reference dataset, especially when hierarchical classification and intermediate/unassigned cell state assignments are desired.
- pitfalls: Using unnormalized reference data (reference data must be normalized beforehand, unlike input data) ;; Retaining highly expressed housekeeping genes (e.g., ribosomal protein genes) which can bias classification ;; Insufficient reference cell counts for sparse data (e.g., 10X Genomics data typically requires 100+ cells per cell type, whereas Smart-Seq2 requires only 10-20) ;; Setting the confidence threshold to 0, which forces all cells to final types but introduces noise and false positives ;; Using a reference dataset from a different biological type or cell state than the input data

workflows.name: cell_type_classification
workflows.intent: Classify single-cell RNA-seq query data using a reference dataset and explore or adjust the classification results.
input: input_counts (matrix of raw scRNA-seq counts for query cells)
input_tsne (matrix of 2D reduced dimensions for query cells)
ref_counts (matrix of normalized scRNA-seq counts for reference cells)
ref_ct (named character vector of cell types for reference cells)
workflows.stages: 1. Create SingleCellExperiment objects for both reference and input data ;; 2. Run the hierarchical classification using CHETAHclassifier ;; 3. Visualize the classification tree and t-SNE map using PlotCHETAH ;; 4. Adjust the classification confidence threshold using Classify ;; 5. Rename intermediate or final cell types using RenameBelowNode ;; 6. Launch the interactive Shiny application using CHETAHshiny
workflows.code:
reference <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = ref_counts),
                                     colData = DataFrame(celltypes = ref_ct))

input <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = input_counts),
                              reducedDims = SimpleList(TSNE = input_tsne))

input <- CHETAHclassifier(input = input, ref_cells = reference)

PlotCHETAH(input)

celltypes <- input$celltype_CHETAH

PlotCHETAH(input = input_mel, interm = TRUE)

colors <- PlotCHETAH(input = input_mel, return_col = TRUE)

CHETAHshiny(input = input_mel)

input_mel <- Classify(input = input_mel, 0.8)
PlotCHETAH(input = input_mel, tree = FALSE)

input_mel <- Classify(input_mel, 0)
PlotCHETAH(input = input_mel, tree = FALSE)

input_mel <- RenameBelowNode(input_mel, whichnode = 6, replacement = "T cell")
PlotCHETAH(input = input_mel, tree = FALSE)

input_mel <- Classify(input_mel)
PlotCHETAH(input = input_mel, tree = FALSE)

workflows.name: reference_qc_and_preparation
workflows.intent: Prepare and evaluate the quality of a reference dataset to ensure optimal cell type classification performance.
input: headneck_ref (SingleCellExperiment object containing reference counts and cell type metadata)
ribosomal.txt (text file containing ribosomal gene names to discard)
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize the reference counts ;; 2. Filter out highly expressed housekeeping/ribosomal genes ;; 3. Correlate reference cell types using CorrelateReference to check distinguishability ;; 4. Perform self-classification of the reference using ClassifyReference to identify potential mix-ups
workflows.code:
assay(headneck_ref, "counts") <- apply(assay(headneck_ref, "counts"), 2, function(column) log2((column/sum(column) * 100000) + 1))

ribo <- read.table("~/ribosomal.txt", header = FALSE, sep = '\t')
headneck_ref <- headneck_ref[!rownames(headneck_ref) %in% ribo[,1], ]

CorrelateReference(ref_cells = headneck_ref)

ClassifyReference(ref_cells = headneck_ref)
